messages:
jia: Quick follow-up from the KV ownership RFC meeting — proposing a lightweight write-lease handshake to avoid cross-region split-writes during failover and eviction. High level: tenant pins a region; that region holds a short-lived lease for writes and serves reads. On eviction or maintenance we hand off the lease with a handshake, otherwise fallback to read-only local cache and async replay.

marta: sketch the handshake steps? want to see edge cases (network partition + residency constraints).

samir: +1 on handshake. sketch: 1) source region sets lease_expiring and writes a signed handoff token; 2) target region validates token and confirms; 3) source marks lease_transferred and stops accepting new writes. token short TTL ~30s.

jia: Here's a minimal token payload we discussed: ```{\n  "tenant_id": "t-1234",\n  "lease_id": "lease-2026-03-12-abc",\n  "from_region": "us-west-2",\n  "to_region": "eu-central-1",\n  "expiry": 1670000000,\n  "sig": "..."\n}``` token must be signed via KMS key per-region and include residency scope.

liam: residency constraints: some tenants must not write outside their resident region. How does handshake respect that?

samir: we should encode residency_policy in token validation: if tenant.residency == "strict" then fail handshake unless to_region == resident_region; if "preferred" allow but log and alert. That way control plane enforces policy.

marta: network partition scenario: if target never confirms, source needs a deterministic fallback. proposal: source flips to read-only mode and continues to accept local ephemeral ops into a write-ahead buffer with per-tenant quarantine tag. When connectivity restored, either handshake resumes or ops are redeemed via ordered replay; otherwise ops are dropped depending on policy.

jia: important operational bits:
- lease TTL short (20–60s) to limit split-write windows
- all writes require lease token validation layer in runtime (fast path).
- introduce a per-tenant flag: allow_async_replay = [true|false] (enforced at control plane).

samir: dev note: runtime needs fast signature check. we can cache KMS public keys and rotate based on key id in token. Include fallback mode where unvalidated writes are rejected with 409 + client hint to retry with region pinned.

liam: can we surface this in Console as a "pending handoff" state for tenants? ops would love visibility.

marta: yes — Console shows lease owner, target, age, and final state (Transferred / Rolled back / Pending). add ability to force-rollback for emergencies.

devops-bot: deploy-check: added initial handshake lambda to staging, route set for us-west-2 -> eu-central-1, tests queued. :white_check_mark:

jia: open questions:
- exact TTL tradeoff (latency vs risk)
- how to surface client-level retry hints without changing SDKs (HTTP header? error code?)
- telemetry: handshake success rate, time-to-transfer, dropped ops per-tenant

samir: I'll draft a small RFC appendix with state machine and pseudocode for runtime checks. assigning to @samir and @marta to iterate.

jia: thanks — rough plan: we iterate appendix, run staging tests, then do a limited canary with cross-region tenants.
